meta.browserPolicy: Committed JSON only; no visitor-time evidence calls

question: Where do rates, prices and leverage turn macro shocks into household, fiscal or financial stress?

verdict.label: Resilient aggregates, concentrated exposure
verdict.text: Dutch household credit was 93.8% of GDP in 2025 Q4, down from 119.0% in 2015 Q4, while the BIS modelled household debt-service ratio was 13.0% of income. Lower aggregate ratios do not remove risk for recent, highly leveraged or liquidity-poor borrowers.
verdict.direction: Debt ratios fell for years, but mortgage borrowing and debt service have stopped improving while new borrowing rates remain well above the ultra-low-rate period.
verdict.distribution: Debt, liquid savings, housing equity and pension claims sit with different households and cannot be netted into a representative balance sheet.

questions: Who is benefiting or carrying the cost?
What evidence would change our current conclusion?

lenses.label: World
lenses.role: BIS cross-country structural credit and debt-service context; coverage is not universal

lenses.label: Europe / Netherlands
lenses.role: Harmonised fiscal, saving, banking and lending definitions

lenses.label: Selected countries
lenses.role: Mechanism contrasts in leverage and rate reset; not a fragility ranking

dimensions.label: Households
dimensions.question: Can income and liquid buffers absorb repayments, inflation and rate resets?
dimensions.doNotConfuse: Debt stock is not debt service; saving flow is not a liquid emergency buffer.

dimensions.label: Government
dimensions.question: Does interest absorb fiscal capacity or force crowd-out?
dimensions.doNotConfuse: Gross debt, net debt, interest/GDP and interest/revenue answer different questions.

dimensions.label: Banks
dimensions.question: Can capital, liquidity and earnings absorb credit and market losses?
dimensions.doNotConfuse: Capital is not liquidity; low NPLs are not a guarantee against future losses.

dimensions.label: Pensions
dimensions.question: Are promised benefits covered through a valuation shock and transition?
dimensions.doNotConfuse: Funding coverage is not benefit adequacy or household liquidity.

balanceSheets.interpretation: A high gross debt stock whose ratio has fallen materially since 2015.
balanceSheets.caveat: GDP is not household income and assets are not netted.

balanceSheets.interpretation: Low relative to the euro-area aggregate, but the interest flow still matters for budgets.
balanceSheets.caveat: Maastricht gross debt is not net debt and does not include every contingent liability.

balanceSheets.interpretation: Loss-absorbing common equity remains substantial in aggregate.
balanceSheets.caveat: A risk-weighted capital ratio is not cash liquidity and masks dispersion.

balanceSheets.interpretation: Aggregate funding improved before the pension-system transition.
balanceSheets.caveat: Coverage does not establish benefit adequacy, indexation or household access.

householdCredit.label: Total credit to households and NPISHs
householdCredit.population: Households and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISH)
householdCredit.denominator: Quarterly nominal GDP, BIS ratio convention
householdCredit.frequency: Quarterly, end of period, not seasonally adjusted

householdDebtService.label: Household and NPISH debt-service ratio
householdDebtService.population: Households and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISH)
householdDebtService.denominator: BIS modelled income available for debt service
householdDebtService.caveat: The BIS applies a unified aggregate model. It is strongest for change over time; absolute country levels are less comparable than within-country movements.

newMortgageRate.label: Rate on new loans for house purchase
newMortgageRate.population: Households and NPISHs; new euro-denominated business
newMortgageRate.denominator: Annualised agreed rate on new business
newMortgageRate.caveat: New-business pricing is not the effective rate on the outstanding mortgage stock and does not reveal each loan's reset date.

householdSaving.label: Gross household saving rate
householdSaving.denominator: Gross disposable income adjusted for change in pension entitlements
householdSaving.caveat: A national saving flow is not a stock of liquid emergency funds and says nothing about who saved.

governmentInterest.label: General-government interest payable
governmentInterest.denominator: Nominal GDP for interest/GDP; total general-government revenue for interest/revenue
governmentInterest.formula: interestToRevenuePct = D41PAY (million EUR) / TR (million EUR) × 100; interestToGdpPct is Eurostat PC_GDP
governmentInterest.caveat: Interest payable is a flow. It is neither gross debt nor the effective yield on debt, and the two displayed ratios use different denominators.

householdDistribution.exposure: Large mortgage relative to income or home value; less time to amortise
householdDistribution.shockChannel: Income loss, refinancing and house-price decline
householdDistribution.evidence: Owners under 35 had average mortgage debt equal to 0.64 of home value in 2024.
householdDistribution.boundary: Average loan-to-value does not reveal debt-service-to-income or tail risk.

householdDistribution.exposure: Fewer liquid and housing assets; high essential spending shares
householdDistribution.shockChannel: Inflation and income loss rather than mortgage reset
householdDistribution.evidence: Median wealth was €1.5k in the lowest income decile versus €520.2k in the highest in 2024.
householdDistribution.boundary: Wealth includes illiquid assets; pension entitlements are excluded from this CBS definition.

householdDistribution.exposure: Often lower mortgage leverage and more housing equity
householdDistribution.shockChannel: Asset repricing, pension indexation and care costs
householdDistribution.evidence: CBS reports that older households often own homes and have largely repaid mortgages.
householdDistribution.boundary: Age averages hide renters, interest-only loans and households without accessible savings.

householdDistribution.exposure: Large deferred claims but limited immediate access
householdDistribution.evidence: Dutch pension funds' aggregate funding ratio was 122.9% at end-2025.
householdDistribution.boundary: Pension claims cannot normally pay today's mortgage or emergency bill.

banks.unit: % of loans excluding central-bank cash and demand deposits
banks.boundary: arrears and Stage 2 exposures use different definitions
EBA sample; Q1 volumes rose only slightly

banks.unit: basis points above OCR + P2G, approximately
banks.boundary: weighted aggregate with wide bank and country dispersion

pensions.boundary: new-system conversion outcomes require fund-level evidence

arrearsBoundary.label: Arrears are not defaults
arrearsBoundary.text: There is no stable, harmonised series in this updater that joins Dutch mortgage payment arrears, consumer-credit arrears and realised defaults with consistent clocks. Bank NPL ratios are therefore shown only as a separate institutional safeguard.
arrearsBoundary.whatWouldResolve: A validated official series with population, days-past-due threshold, cure policy, loan count or balance denominator, and revision history.

explanations.label: Leverage
explanations.text: Large debts amplify income and valuation shocks even when collateral initially exceeds the loan.
explanations.test: Track debt-to-income, loan-to-value and liquid buffers jointly by borrower cohort.

explanations.label: Income shock
explanations.text: Job loss or real-income compression can create payment stress without a rate reset.
explanations.test: Match repayment problems to income transitions and essential-cost exposure.

explanations.label: Rate reset
explanations.text: New-business rates reveal the price facing new borrowers, not how quickly the outstanding stock reprices.
explanations.test: Publish the stock by remaining fixation period, income and loan-to-value.

explanations.label: Inflation
explanations.text: Inflation can erode real fixed debt while simultaneously compressing disposable cash flow and lifting rates.
explanations.test: Separate nominal debt relief from the household budget effect.

explanations.label: Housing scarcity
explanations.text: Scarcity supports collateral values but can force new buyers toward larger loans.
explanations.test: Join local supply, prices, borrower leverage and tenure.

explanations.label: Market repricing
explanations.text: Fast yield or asset-price moves can expose duration and liquidity mismatches before credit defaults rise.
explanations.test: Use institution-level stress tests; market volatility alone is not structural indebtedness.

reversalIndicators.label: Persistent household defaults
reversalIndicators.threshold: A broad, sustained rise in consistently defined defaults after cures and write-offs
reversalIndicators.meaning: Aggregate debt-service resilience would no longer describe borrower outcomes.

reversalIndicators.label: Depleted liquid buffers
reversalIndicators.threshold: Falling deposits or liquid assets concentrated among mortgagors and low-income households
reversalIndicators.meaning: The saving-flow comfort would be contradicted by household-level stocks.

reversalIndicators.label: Fiscal crowd-out
reversalIndicators.threshold: Interest/revenue rises persistently while productive or protective spending is displaced
reversalIndicators.meaning: Low gross debt would cease to imply ample fiscal room.

reversalIndicators.label: Bank losses
reversalIndicators.threshold: NPL, Stage 2 and realised-loss ratios rise as capital headroom and liquidity fall
reversalIndicators.meaning: Safeguards would be absorbing rather than merely standing ready for stress.

reversalIndicators.label: Restored affordability
reversalIndicators.threshold: New-borrower payments fall relative to income without looser risk layering
reversalIndicators.meaning: Household leverage would become easier to service rather than only smaller relative to GDP.

reversalIndicators.label: Pension resilience
reversalIndicators.threshold: Funding and expected benefits remain stable through transition and valuation shocks
reversalIndicators.meaning: Deferred household claims would be more defensible as a long-run buffer.

dataGaps: Dutch arrears and defaults with a stable days-past-due clock, balance denominator and cure policy.
Mortgage stock by remaining rate-fixation period joined to borrower income, age, tenure and liquid assets.
Government contingent liabilities and refinancing schedule joined to interest/revenue scenarios.
Fund-level pension coverage joined to expected benefit adequacy and transition outcomes.
Comparable household liquid emergency buffers; aggregate saving and deposits cannot supply this distribution.

sources.title: Credit to the non-financial sector
sources.denominatorUnit: Percentage of GDP; end-of-period credit stock; market value; adjusted for breaks
sources.methodology: Total core debt from all lending sectors, following the System of National Accounts; quarterly nominal-GDP ratio.
sources.transformation: Updater filters the exact seven-dimension key, sorts periods and rounds observations to one decimal.
sources.revisionPolicy: Refresh quarterly; revisions replace the full baked series after definition and chronology validation.
sources.interpretation: Shows structural indebtedness relative to the economy.
sources.caveat: Household includes NPISH; gross credit is not net wealth, household income or debt service.

sources.title: Debt service ratios
sources.denominatorUnit: Percent of modelled income available for debt service
sources.methodology: BIS unified aggregate model combines debt, income, average interest rate and remaining maturity to estimate interest plus amortisation.
sources.transformation: Updater filters the exact key, sorts periods and rounds to one decimal.
sources.revisionPolicy: Refresh quarterly; review methodology changes before publishing.
sources.interpretation: Best read as within-country movement in debt-service constraints.
sources.caveat: Modelled aggregate level is not a microdata payment-to-income distribution and country levels are difficult to compare.

sources.institution: European Central Bank / De Nederlandsche Bank
sources.title: MFI interest rates: new loans to households for house purchase
sources.geographyPopulation: Netherlands; households and NPISH; new euro-denominated mortgage business
sources.denominatorUnit: Percent per annum, annualised agreed rate / narrowly defined effective rate
sources.methodology: Deposit-taking corporations excluding the central bank; all initial fixation periods and amount categories.
sources.transformation: Updater filters the exact series key, sorts monthly observations and rounds to two decimals.
sources.revisionPolicy: Refresh monthly; replace history after key and unit validation.
sources.interpretation: Shows marginal borrowing cost faced by new business.
sources.caveat: Not the effective rate, reset schedule or debt service of the outstanding stock.

sources.title: Key indicators: gross household saving rate
sources.denominatorUnit: Gross saving / (gross disposable income adjusted for pension-entitlement changes), percent
sources.methodology: ESA 2010 sector accounts key indicator: B8G / (B6G + D8rec − D8pay) × 100.
sources.transformation: Updater filters SRG_S14_S15 for NL, annual frequency, then sorts and rounds to one decimal.
sources.revisionPolicy: Refresh annually; preserve historical revisions after dimension checks.
sources.interpretation: Shows the national flow not consumed from adjusted disposable income.
sources.caveat: Saving flow is not liquid wealth, an emergency buffer or a distribution.

sources.title: Government revenue, expenditure and main aggregates
sources.seriesTableId: gov_10a_main; S13; D41PAY and TR; units MIO_EUR and PC_GDP
sources.denominatorUnit: Interest payable in million EUR and percent of GDP; total revenue in million EUR
sources.methodology: ESA 2010 government finance statistics for D.41 payable interest and total revenue.
sources.transformation: interest/revenue = D41PAY MIO_EUR ÷ TR MIO_EUR × 100; interest/GDP uses Eurostat PC_GDP directly.
sources.revisionPolicy: Refresh after April/October transmissions; recalculate derived ratios from unrounded inputs.
sources.interpretation: Shows the budgetary interest flow with two explicit denominators.
sources.caveat: Interest/GDP and interest/revenue have separate denominators and are not the government debt stock.

sources.title: Government deficit and debt: gross consolidated government debt
sources.denominatorUnit: Maastricht gross consolidated debt as percent of GDP
sources.methodology: Excessive Deficit Procedure table for general-government gross consolidated debt at nominal value.
sources.transformation: Updater filters NL, S13, GD and PC_GDP, sorts annual periods and rounds to one decimal.
sources.revisionPolicy: Refresh after EDP transmissions; preserve historical revisions after exact dimension checks.
sources.interpretation: Shows the gross government debt stock relative to GDP.
sources.caveat: Maastricht gross debt is not net debt and excludes some contingent liabilities.

sources.title: Supervisory banking statistics: significant institutions
sources.seriesTableId: Q1 2026 overview; CET1 ratio and NPL ratio
sources.geographyPopulation: Significant institutions in European banking supervision
sources.denominatorUnit: CET1 / risk-weighted assets; NPL / loans excluding central-bank cash and demand deposits
sources.methodology: Aggregated COREP and FINREP reports at the relevant consolidation level.
sources.transformation: Manual snapshot of published aggregate ratios; no combination with EBA sample.
sources.revisionPolicy: Manual quarterly review because sample and definitions require audit.
sources.interpretation: Shows aggregate loss absorption and recognised problem loans.
sources.caveat: Capital is not liquidity; risk weights and aggregate ratios mask institution dispersion.

sources.title: Risk Dashboard Q1 2026 and Risk Assessment Report Spring 2026
sources.seriesTableId: RDB Q1 2026 statistical annex; RAR figures 2, 3, 25, 26, 43
sources.geographyPopulation: EU/EEA supervisory sample; 161 banks from 30 EEA countries in the RAR
sources.period: 2025-Q4 stock metrics with Q1 2026 direction and capital-headroom observation
sources.denominatorUnit: Metric-specific: NPL / total loans; capital headroom in basis points; liquidity and profitability separately defined
sources.role: Bank resilience, dispersion and emerging-loss context
sources.methodology: EBA supervisory reporting uses weighted averages and an unbalanced sample unless stated otherwise.
sources.transformation: Manual, review-gated snapshot from the annex/report; metrics are not combined.
sources.revisionPolicy: Manual quarterly annex review; preserve sample and metric definition with every value.
sources.interpretation: Capital and liquidity start from strength while risks remain concentrated.
sources.caveat: NPLs, Stage 2, CET1, liquidity and profitability are different dimensions; country and bank dispersion is wide.

sources.title: Distribution of well-being: material well-being
sources.denominatorUnit: Median and aggregate euros by household income group; pension entitlements excluded
sources.methodology: CBS income and wealth statistics; assets less liabilities under the published household-wealth definition.
sources.transformation: Manual transcription of published medians and definition.
sources.interpretation: Shows why aggregate assets cannot be assumed to sit with indebted households.
sources.caveat: Wealth is not liquidity; pension entitlements are excluded and home values are illiquid.

sources.title: SDG 10.2 Financial sustainability
sources.seriesTableId: Average mortgage debt and debt/home-value ratio for owners under 35
sources.geographyPopulation: Netherlands; households with mortgages and owner-occupiers under 35
sources.denominatorUnit: Euros per mortgaged household; mortgage debt / home value
sources.methodology: Integral Income and Assets Survey and national accounts; metric-specific populations.
sources.transformation: Manual snapshot; no aggregation across populations.
sources.interpretation: Younger owners remain a useful leverage-exposure lens.
sources.caveat: Loan-to-value is not payment-to-income, liquidity, arrears or default.

sources.title: DNB Annual Report 2025: pension fund funding ratio
sources.seriesTableId: Pension funds average funding ratio at year-end
sources.geographyPopulation: Dutch pension funds under DNB supervision
sources.methodology: Aggregate regulatory funding ratio under the applicable pension framework.
sources.revisionPolicy: Manual quarterly/annual review through the system transition.
sources.interpretation: Indicates aggregate coverage of measured pension liabilities.
sources.caveat: Funding coverage is not benefit adequacy, indexation, fund-level dispersion or liquid household wealth.
